title: Replicating DARPA AIxCC-Style Vulnerability Detection on a Low-Resource Budget

original_idea.body:
# Replicating DARPA AIxCC-Style Vulnerability Detection on a Low-Resource Budget

**Problem:** DARPA AIxCC teams had large resources. The winning team cost ~$152 per task at competition scale. Can AIxCC-style vulnerability detection be replicated at student-scale cost (< $50 total API spend)?

**Direction:** Select 10 synthetic vulnerability scenarios inspired by AIxCC challenge design (memory corruption, logic flaws, injection). Implement a minimal AI-assisted detection pipeline using Claude or GPT-4o API with strict token budgeting. Measure detection rate vs. cost. Compare to AIxCC results.

**Why it matters:** If high-quality vulnerability detection requires large resources, small defenders (open-source projects, NGOs, small companies) cannot benefit from AI defense. Demonstrating low-cost equivalents democratizes defense.

**Relevant context:** DARPA AIxCC 2025: $152/task average cost. SoK AIxCC paper (arXiv 2602.07666). Trail of Bits Buttercup architecture. Student-scale replication not attempted.
